ideas.description: Exploit the flat per-epoch slope. E010 gave 0.31 pp/epoch and E017 gave 0.11 pp/epoch near 11 epochs, so cutting epochs may be the cheapest lever left. Start from the incumbent E012 (commit 6d40ead: 128/256/576, 3 convs per block, translate 2, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph, 11 epochs). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 10, and rescale the LR/Lookahead schedule to the new step count so it still anneals fully. Report per-seed accuracy and the per-seed minimum. This measures this net's slope between 10 and 11 epochs: H1.1.4 asks the slope question of the wide net, and this asks it of the incumbent. If I023 (96/256/576) becomes the new tip first, apply the same 1-epoch cut to that tip instead.
ideas.expected: Time about 7.0 s (7.70 x 10/11, -9%). Accuracy -0.15 to -0.6 pp, to about 0.751-0.755. If accuracy >= 0.753, this is a new best and the next step is 9.5 epochs. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, the slope below 11 epochs is steep (>= 0.4 pp/epoch, unlike the flat slope above it), so the next try is 10.5 epochs. If it falls below 0.750, epochs stay at 11 and margin has to come from elsewhere.

ideas.description: Combine near-misses: put block-3 capacity into the resize recipe. E012 suggests block-3 width is the capacity that 100 classes need. E013 and E017 sit 0.1-0.2 pp short, and extra epochs barely help there (E017 gave +0.11 pp/epoch). Start from E013 (commit b0eba3b: 128/256/576, 11 epochs, first 50% of steps at 24 px via bilinear antialias=True, translate 2, both shapes compiled and graphed in build; 0.7510 at 6.32 s). Change only block-3 width, from 576 to 704 (3 convs per block, head input widened to match). Block 3 runs at 8x8 (4x4 or 6x6 maps during the 24 px phase), so per-image conv MACs rise only ~0.2 G (~+15%).
ideas.expected: Time +0.3 to +0.45 s, to about 6.6-6.8 s. Accuracy +0.2 to +0.5 pp, to about 0.753-0.756. If feasible, this is ~12-14% faster than E012, which supports 'block-3 width is the binding capacity' and the H5 ceiling view: width raises the ceiling where epochs could not. A gain under 0.15 pp means block 3 is not binding either, and the resize line is capped near 0.752 for this family.

ideas.description: A smaller low-res fraction on the incumbent. All resize schedules so far land on ~0.4 pp lost per second saved (E008/E013/E018), and the cost seems to scale with the FLOPs removed. A 25% fraction uses that line where E012 has margin (0.37 pp). Start from E012 (11 epochs, translate 2). Change only the resolution schedule: the first 25% of steps run at 24 px (bilinear F.interpolate, antialias=True, after flip and translate, inside the compiled and graphed step); the rest run at 32 px. Capture both shapes in build and check that no recompile lands in timed train. This is the alternative to the epoch-cut idea for the same ~0.7 s: if both run, compare their pp lost per second saved.
ideas.expected: Time about -0.65 to -0.75 s, to about 6.95-7.05 s. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.35 pp, to about 0.753-0.755. Feasible means a new best, unless the epoch cut is cheaper per second. If the loss per second saved is < 0.3 pp/s, the resize cost is front-loaded or non-linear, so small fractions are efficient; ~0.4 pp/s confirms the linear line.

ideas.description: Schedule constant tuned for long runs. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), change only the LR schedule end point: linear decay to 5% of peak instead of to 0, with warmup, Lookahead and everything else unchanged. Precompute the per-step LR the same way as now so the CUDA graph is unchanged. This is the decisive test of H4.5.1; the fulcrum CIFAR-10 champion uses an LR floor.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.15 to +0.3 pp (direction uncertain; without an EMA tail, a nonzero final LR may hurt). Time unchanged (7.70 +/- 0.05 s). A gain of 0.25 pp or more banks margin for the epoch cut and supports H4.5. A loss of 0.15 pp or more refutes H4.5.1 and keeps decay to 0.

ideas.description: Follow-up to E015, which showed the regime is sample-limited, not step-limited: going from batch 1024 to 768 left accuracy flat and cost +5% time. Test whether a larger batch buys throughput. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), change only the batch size, from 1024 to 1536. Keep the per-example LR and wd as airbench defines them (per-step LR x1.5), tie the schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -5%, to about 7.3-7.55 s (fewer, larger, better-utilized steps). Accuracy -0.05 to -0.35 pp, since there are ~33% fewer steps (~36 per epoch). If accuracy stays >= 0.753 and time falls >= 0.15 s, this is a new best and batch 1536 becomes the default. A time gain under 1.5% means the A100 is already saturated at 1024, which closes the batch axis.

ideas.description: One decisive optimizer check. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), replace Nesterov SGD on the block conv filters (not the whitening layer, BN or head) with Muon in the airbench94_muon form: Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov. BN, biases and head stay on the current SGD with the current schedule. Lookahead stays as it is. Run Newton-Schulz in bf16 inside the compiled step and capture it in build. Prepare must reset the Muon momentum buffers.
ideas.expected: Expected outcome: refuted. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.3 pp; time +3 to +8% (Newton-Schulz on 576x5184 matrices). A gain of 0.3 pp or more at a time cost under 4% would reopen the optimizer axis as an epoch-cut enabler. Otherwise close H4.2.

structured_output.summary:
The incumbent is E012 (128/256/576, 11 epochs, translate 2): 0.7567 accuracy at 7.70 s, which is 0.37 pp of margin over 0.753. Three findings shape the new ideas:
- Every resize schedule lands on the same line of ~0.4 pp lost per second saved.
- Extra epochs near 11 return almost nothing (0.1-0.3 pp per epoch), so cutting epochs may be cheap.
- Block-3 width looks like the binding capacity.

New ideas:
- **Priority 5, cut epochs 11 to 10 on E012:** directly exploits the flat slope. Expected about 7.0 s at 0.751-0.755.
- **Priority 4, widen block 3 to 704 on E013:** combines two near-misses. Width may raise the ceiling where epochs could not (E017). Expected about 6.7 s at 0.753-0.756.
- **Priority 3, 25% of steps at 24 px on E012:** buys the same ~0.7 s through resize instead of epochs. Comparing the two gives each lever's cost per second saved.
- **Priority 3, LR floor at 5% of peak (H4.5.1):** an untested Lvl3 schedule change that could bank margin.
- **Priority 3, batch 1536:** follows E015's finding that the regime is sample-limited, so a larger batch may buy throughput.
- **Priority 2, Muon (H4.2.1):** one decisive check, expected to be refuted.

I keep I024 (fused foreach optimizer in the captured graph) and I025 (data-path warm-up in build). Both are cheap tests of throughput with the same math. The committee's unanimous 'not-improved' vote on them is outside the evidence, and I025 can be read directly from the per-trial prepare times.

Note that several queue descriptions (I021, I022, I023) say "translate 4". Per the I019/I020 notes, the tip lineage from E011 onward uses translate 2, and the new ideas say so explicitly.

The queue is now 8 queued ideas plus I023 running. If I023 (96/256/576) wins, the epoch-cut idea is rebased onto it.
